text:
Alex: Quick heads-up: ran a long-running streaming soak on canary v2-quant and hit a persistent tail starting ~13:10 UTC. Host preparse threads burned CPU and we saw allocator/fragment growth.
Maria: Any flamegraphs/profiles? which funcs look hot?
Alex: Uploaded a short trace. Top of stack: socket_reader -> framer::coalesce_read -> parse::assemble_header -> kv::get_or_load -> kernel_selector::choose_fallback. Notably lots of tiny reads (40-250B).

```
# trace summary
13:09:58 socket read loop -> 140ms
13:10:02 frame assemble  -> 360ms (realloc)
13:10:02 kv get_or_load -> 230ms (miss storm)
13:10:03 kernel fallback-> 100ms
13:10:03 decode queue   -> 500ms (small-batch queuing)
```

Alex: Kernel selector is preferring a narrow-kernel when batching heuristics see many small inflight requests. That reduces GPU throughput and pushes work back to host threads.
Sam: Could be that the framer is yielding too eagerly: Nagle disabled on some test clients means we get many small TCP segs. Are they using gRPC HTTP/2 streaming or raw socket?
Alex: gRPC (HTTP/2) streaming from our load lab, token-by-token style. Hypothesis: 1) framer doesn't coalesce enough; 2) KV cache shards get hot and cause per-shard lock contention under the small-batch fallback.
Jen: We had a recent rollback of framer coalesce flag (stream_coalesce_ms) because of a separate latency regression. Any chance raising it slightly helps?
Alex: I tried a local run with stream_coalesce_ms=9ms and a 1kB soft threshold. Results: coalesced bytes up, decode queue latency down ~25%, throughput +9%. CPU dropped on preparse threads but kernel_select overhead rose slightly.
Perf-bot: Canary note: test-canary/813 -> stream_coalesce_ms set to 9ms at 13:35 UTC for perf testing.

Maria: Good. We should validate KV behavior: is eviction policy LRU per-shard? what's shard assignment?
Sam: It's sharded LRU with mod-based shard hash. Small, skewed keys can overload single shard. If small batches change access patterns, we might observe frequent cross-shard misses and lock waits.
Alex: I instrumented per-shard miss and lock wait: three shards had >60% of locks under that run. Lock wait accounted for ~18% of preparse thread time.
Jen: Mitigations to try: bump coalesce to 8-12ms (canary), add a tiny connection-level prefetch for probable kv prefixes on new streams, or randomize shard assignment for high-frequency keys. Also change batching heuristics to favor 5ms or 1kB aggregation before selecting narrow kernels.
Alex: Quick patch I used locally (pseudo):

```
// framer: wait up to coalesce_ms or until buffer >= threshold
if (buf.len() < COALESCE_THRESHOLD && elapsed < coalesce_ms) {
  poll_socket_for_more(timeout = coalesce_ms - elapsed);
}
parse(buf);
```

Sam: Add metric "framer.coalesced_bytes" and "kv.shard_lock_wait_ms" so we can tune without trial-and-error.
Maria: Agree. Also include a guard in canary rollout to auto-fallback the coalesce flag if p50/p95 or token success rate degrades.
Perf-bot: Created ticket PERF-1428: RFC for framer coalesce + batching heuristic + KV shard sim.

Alex: Action items: I'll open RFC with flamegraphs and the small patch + perf numbers. Sam will run a KV-shard skew simulator to test alternative assignments. Jen will wire the canary rollback guard and add metrics to the dashboard.
Maria: I'll review the RFC and help with acceptance criteria for canary. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks — ping me if you want to pair on the simulator.
